response: No, Pap smears with glandular cell abnormalities are often not detected by rapid prescreening. Glandular cell abnormalities can be more challenging to identify and may require a more thorough and detailed review of the Pap smear sample. Rapid prescreening is typically used to identify obvious squamous cell abnormalities, but it may not be as effective in detecting glandular cell abnormalities, which can be more subtle and require a more expert review.
